key_insight: An agentic AI workflow links liver lesion segmentation to structured radiology reports using traceable measurements and numerical consistency checks.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help translate imaging predictions into interpretable reports, but clinical utility remains to be established.
method: TotalSegmentator-based nnU-Net models segment the liver, Couinaud segments, and lesions.
Deterministic tools calculate volumes, dimensions, lesion counts, and anatomical locations.
An LLM organizes measurements into a predefined report schema with numerical consistency checks.
evidence_signal: Across 51 LiTS cases, liver Dice was 0.947, lesion sensitivity 75.6%, and positive predictive value 68.9%; separate exploratory screening found liver-related abnormalities in 10,208 of 25,494 MERLIN reports (40.0%).
watch_item: Incomplete lesion detection and false positives warrant expert review; the abstract does not report end-to-end clinical validation of generated reports.
paper_title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Liver Lesion Segmentation and Structured Radiology Reporting
